loader.method: closed baseline copied with source-root retool.py; no import or function creation

claims.conclusion: Foreign-owner buffer loads open a task-index shared-memory object read-only and mmap recorded length read-only/shared. Same-owner loads use the recorded task pointer instead. These paths need not consult disk.

Normal foreign mmap success branches to buffered restore without the close at 0x1ca4a. That sole direct close call is in foreign open/map failure handling. There is no direct munmap call in this function. Normal completion only unlocks and destroys the persistence guard before returning. No local release of the successful foreign fd/mapping is visible.

Worker cleanup unmaps task+0x180 using task+0x184 length, clears these fields, closes task+0x17c when nonnegative and sets it to -1, then stores state 0 and posts capacity. These are worker task resources, not the foreign loader stack locals. State 0/capacity release are not proof of destination success or a disk/cache freshness barrier.

Repeated successful foreign loads may retain per-load fd/mapping resources until external cleanup or process exit. This function does not reuse the retained foreign mapping as a cache: it opens/maps again on each foreign branch. Actual accumulation, exhaustion and cleanup elsewhere require runtime checks; no leak rate is asserted.

limits: Only selected local bodies and normal control flow audited; not an exhaustive interprocedural exception/callback audit.
State-6 producer and intended semantic meaning unresolved; do not assign an enum name.
No firmware execution, device access or private captures. No runtime quiescence, multi-file atomicity or power-loss durability claim.
